title: Dalton Caldwell on revenue multiples: why comps and market size decide your startup's valuation
summary: Dalton and Paul of Standard Capital explain why public-market revenue multiples set the ceiling for startup valuations. Key warning: AI-enabled service companies get valued like the legacy service firms they disrupt unless founders prove a technology-sized, growing market.

principles.text: Public-market multiples for your category flow downstream into what startups in that category can raise at.
principles.quote: a lot of SaaS companies are trading horribly. Like their their revenue multiples are very low and it's bad and that downwind effect totally hurts startups that are doing SaaS because those are the the comparables that they are valued against, right?

principles.text: Know your comps before you pitch. Research what comparable companies are worth and have a story for why you will be worth far more.
principles.quote: I do think that's an exercise every should do is do the research on what the comparables are and how they are valued and then have a really good story on why you're going to be worth way more than those if the comparables aren't great.

principles.text: AI-enabled service startups risk being valued like the low-multiple service firms they replace; you must prove you deserve tech multiples.
principles.quote: you need to have proof points and a story on why you should be valued as a technology company with technology company multiples, and not as the service company you're disrupting.

principles.text: Legacy service companies trade at roughly 1x to 2x revenue, so a service-like startup can be worth very little even with real revenue.
principles.quote: So, a 2x revenue multiple on a million dollars a year is the company's worth $2 million.

principles.text: High multiples go to businesses that can grow into an unbounded market, not a fixed-size one.
principles.quote: It makes sense that SpaceX would trade at a high multiple versus it being this like fixed finite thing where there's no way it can grow, so it's valued like one or two X.

principles.text: Valuation reflects expected future cash flows, which is why a company can look overvalued for a long time while the market prices in future potential.
principles.quote: the market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent.
